subject: History
description: Akbar's NAVRATNAS — nine jewels of his court: Birbal, Tansen, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Todar Mal, Man Singh I, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Mulla Do-Piyaza, Hakim Humam.

questions.stem: Which of Akbar's NAVRATNAS was famous as a court musician and singer?
questions.explanation: MIYAN TANSEN (originally Ramtanu Pandey, ~1500-1589) — one of Akbar's NAVRATNAS, regarded as the GREATEST musician in Indian history. Born in Behat, near Gwalior; trained under Swami Haridas of Vrindavan. Joined Akbar's court ~1562; granted title 'MIYAN' by Akbar. CONTRIBUTIONS: (1) Created RAGAS — Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar, Darbari Kanada (still core of Hindustani classical music). (2) Master of DHRUPAD style. (3) Legend: Tansen sang Raga Deepak which lit oil lamps; Raga Megh Malhar to bring rain (mythological). DEATH: 1589; Akbar attended his funeral. SAMADHI: at Gwalior (annual Tansen Music Festival held there). LINEAGE: founder of the SENI GHARANA — many great musicians trace lineage to him (e.g., Ustad Bismillah Khan claims artistic ancestry). AKBAR'S NAVRATNAS — full list: (1) Birbal — wit/advisor. (2) Tansen — musician. (3) Abul Fazl — biographer (Akbarnama, Ain-i-Akbari). (4) Faizi — Persian poet, Abul Fazl's brother. (5) Todar Mal — revenue minister (Zabt system). (6) Raja Man Singh I — military general (Amber). (7) Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan — poet, military leader, son of Bairam Khan. (8) Mulla Do-Piyaza — court humorist. (9) Hakim Humam — physician. PYQ FREQUENCY: Navratnas appear in SSC CGL, UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Who among Akbar's Navratnas wrote the AKBARNAMA and AIN-I-AKBARI?
questions.explanation: ABUL FAZL ibn MUBARAK (1551-1602) — Akbar's chief biographer, vizier, and one of the Navratnas. WORKS: (1) AKBARNAMA — three-volume official chronicle of Akbar's reign in PERSIAN; the first two volumes cover history; the THIRD volume is the famous AIN-I-AKBARI ('Institutes of Akbar'). (2) AIN-I-AKBARI — comprehensive administrative report of Akbar's empire — including detailed accounts of revenue, military, court life, geography, weights/measures, statistics. Considered the gazetteer of Mughal India. ABUL FAZL'S BACKGROUND: father Sheikh Mubarak was a learned scholar; brother FAIZI was court poet. Abul Fazl was a champion of DIN-I-ILAHI (Akbar's syncretic religion, 1582) and tolerance — drew strong opposition from orthodox ulema. DEATH: assassinated at age 51 (1602) by VIR SINGH BUNDELA on the orders of PRINCE SALIM (Jahangir) — who resented Abul Fazl's influence over Akbar. KEY VALUE for HISTORIANS: Akbarnama remains one of the MOST DETAILED primary sources for Mughal history. Photographs of original manuscript pages (with Abul Fazl's elegant Persian) are in libraries worldwide. PYQ FREQUENCY: Akbarnama-Abul-Fazl link is a top UPSC, SSC CGL, NCERT staple.

questions.stem: RAJA TODAR MAL is famous for which administrative achievement under Akbar?
questions.explanation: RAJA TODAR MAL (1500-1589) — Akbar's REVENUE MINISTER (Diwan-i-Ashraf). Reformed the Mughal land revenue system, creating what's called the ZABT or DAHSALA system (1580). KEY PRINCIPLES: (1) MEASUREMENT of all cultivable land using a uniform unit (BIGHA). (2) CLASSIFICATION of land by FERTILITY: Polaj (annually cultivated), Parauti (rested), Chachar (fallow 3-4 yrs), Banjar (uncultivable for 5+ yrs). (3) FIXED TAX RATES based on AVERAGE PRICES of crops over previous TEN YEARS — hence DAH-SALA (Persian for 'ten years'). (4) Tax = ~ONE-THIRD of produce, payable in cash or kind. (5) Created the office of QANUNGO (record-keeper). KEY CONTRIBUTION: brought stability, predictability, and reduced peasant exploitation. Land records became extensive. PRECURSORS: SHER SHAH SURI's earlier reforms (1540s) were the foundation; Todar Mal extended and codified them. KEY TEXT: TODAR MAL also coordinated the translation of the MAHABHARATA into Persian (RAZMNAMA project). LATER: Todar Mal was elevated as Wazir; administered Bengal post-conquest. NOTABLE: a learned man fluent in Persian, Sanskrit, mathematics. PYQ FREQUENCY: Todar Mal-revenue link is a top SSC CGL, UPSC, MPSC fact — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: BIRBAL's original name was Mahesh Das. He served Akbar as a:
questions.explanation: BIRBAL (Mahesh Das, ~1528-1586) — RAJA Birbal — served as a WITTY ADVISOR and confidant of Akbar; held the title 'Raja' and the rank of military commander too. ORIGIN: born to a poor Brahmin family at Kanpur. Joined Akbar's court ~1556; rose due to wit, intelligence, and Persian-Hindi-Sanskrit fluency. ROLE: known for his SHARP REPARTEE, problem-solving wit, and ability to entertain the emperor — recorded in countless folk stories ('Akbar-Birbal' tales). RELIGIOUS POSITION: one of the few HINDUS to embrace DIN-I-ILAHI (Akbar's syncretic religion). DEATH: killed in 1586 in the YUSUFZAI Expedition (Afghanistan) — leading a Mughal force; ambushed and slaughtered with most of his troops. Akbar reportedly mourned for days. ACADEMIC CONSENSUS: Birbal's reputation as 'court jester' is largely FOLKLORE; in real history, he was a SERIOUS COMMANDER and political advisor, not merely a comedic figure. Many of the witty tales were composed long after his death. RECENT POPULAR CULTURE: numerous TV shows ('Akbar-Birbal'), films, comics. PYQ FREQUENCY: Birbal-Mahesh-Das identity test in SSC CGL, UPSC 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests beyond-folklore knowledge of Mughal courtiers.

questions.stem: Which of Akbar's Navratnas was a Hindu poet famous for couplets in BRAJ BHASHA?
questions.explanation: ABDUL RAHIM KHAN-I-KHANAN (1556-1627) — son of BAIRAM KHAN (Akbar's regent). Despite being MUSLIM, he wrote prolific BRAJ BHASHA (Hindi dialect) DOHAS (couplets) — pen name 'RAHIM'. He's celebrated alongside KABIR, TULSIDAS, SURDAS as a major Bhakti-period poet. FAMOUS DOHAS: 'Rahiman dhaaga prem ka, mat todo chatkay; Toote se phir naa jude, jude gaanth padi jaay' (don't break the thread of love; once broken, even when rejoined, a knot remains). 'Rahiman paani rakhiye, bin paani sab soon; paani gaye na ubre, moti, manus, choon' (preserve water/honor; without it, pearl, person, lime are useless). MILITARY ROLE: Akbar's COMMANDER — led campaigns in Gujarat, conquered Sindh; later served Jahangir. Held title 'KHAN-I-KHANAN' (Khan of Khans). LANGUAGES: Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit, Turkish, Hindi, Braj. Translated BABURNAMA from Turkish to Persian. TOMB: built for himself in Delhi (now restored, near Humayun's tomb). LATER FATE: lost favor with Jahangir, died in poverty 1627. RAHIM is part of the Hindi school syllabus across India — students memorize his dohas. PYQ FREQUENCY: Rahim is a top UPSC, NCERT, MPSC fact — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: RAJA MAN SINGH I, one of Akbar's Navratnas, was the ruler of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: RAJA MAN SINGH I (1550-1614) — ruler of AMBER (Amer; modern-day Jaipur was founded later by his descendant Sawai Jai Singh II, 1727). KACHHWAHA RAJPUT clan. RELATIONSHIP TO AKBAR: nephew of Bharmal of Amber whose daughter Harkha Bai (Jodha Bai) married Akbar 1562 — so Man Singh became Akbar's grand-nephew by marriage. MILITARY CAREER: Mughal commander; led campaigns in Kabul, Bengal, Bihar, Orissa. KEY BATTLE — HALDIGHATI (1576): commanded Mughal forces against MAHARANA PRATAP of Mewar; tactical Mughal victory but Pratap escaped to continue resistance. ROLE: Mansabdar of 7000 (highest Hindu rank under Akbar); one of the FOUR PILLARS of empire (with Abul Fazl, Birbal, Todar Mal). RELIGIOUS: HINDU; Akbar's tolerance allowed top Hindu generals; built temples (Govind Dev temple in Vrindavan). DEATH: 1614 (Jahangir's reign). SUCCESSION: Amber kingdom continued; Sawai Jai Singh II (1693-1743) founded JAIPUR city (1727) with Vidyadhar Bhattacharya as architect. JAIPUR is the largest planned city of pre-modern India. CONTRAST — MEWAR (Udaipur) under Maharana Pratap RESISTED Mughals; Amber ALLIED with them — strategic disagreement among Rajputs. PYQ FREQUENCY: Man Singh-Amber link in SSC, UPSC.

questions.stem: FAIZI, one of Akbar's Navratnas, was famous as a:

options.option_text: Builder of major Mughal forts (option here)

questions.explanation: ABUL FAIZ FAIZI (1547-1595) — elder brother of ABUL FAZL; appointed Akbar's COURT POET (Malik-ush-Shu'ara, 1588). PERSIAN POETRY: composed ~101 books, famous for ELEGIES (marsiyas), ghazals, qasidas. Translated MAHABHARATA's BHISHMA PARVA from Sanskrit. Also translated LILAVATI (the famous Sanskrit math text by Bhaskaracharya) into Persian. NOTED WORKS: NAL-DAMAYANTI (Persian retelling of the Sanskrit love story); MARKAZ-I-ADWAR (rhetoric treatise). FAMILY BACKGROUND: father Sheikh Mubarak was a Sufi-influenced scholar; the family was hounded by orthodox ulema for liberal views. Faizi & Abul Fazl became core figures in Akbar's RELIGIOUS TOLERANCE policies. DEATH: 1595, age 48; broke Akbar's heart. AFTER FAIZI: Abul Fazl became Akbar's closest confidant. CONTRAST WITH OTHER POETS: Faizi was Persian poet; RAHIM was Braj Bhasha poet; both contemporaries. KEY EXAMPLE LINE: 'Be sure that your tongue does not utter that which your heart does not approve' (translated). HISTORICAL: Faizi's works survive in libraries (Bodleian, Tehran, Hyderabad). PYQ FREQUENCY: Faizi as poet/translator appears in UPSC History optional, NCERT-driven SSC 1× per cycle.
